f.title: Review participant safety in a timely manner as new safety information emerges

rows.review_note: Review: quote extended (with the page footer text verbatim) back to the 1.4.8 lead-in so actor ("investigator/institution"), "promptly" and should-level are proven; items (a)-(b) stay in 0003/0005; processes intake replaced by communications (outbound reporting to IRB/IEC). f.title: Inform participants promptly of new information relevant to their willingness to continue and document it
f.statement: The participant or legally acceptable representative should be informed in a timely manner if new information becomes available that may be relevant to the participant's willingness to continue trial participation; the communication and confirmation of willingness to continue should be documented. Such information should be assessed to determine whether re-consent is needed; where re-consent is needed (e.g. emerging safety concerns), the new information should be clearly identified in revised informed consent materials, which need IRB/IEC approval/favourable opinion before use.
f.clause: III. Annex 1, 2.8.2 Informed Consent of Trial Participants
f.processes: Clinical safety monitoring; Safety communications

rows.deadline: In a timely manner once new information becomes available
rows.quote: The participant or the participant’s legally acceptable representative should be informed in a timely manner if new information becomes available that may be relevant to the participant’s willingness to continue trial participation. The communication of this information and confirmation of the willingness to continue trial participation should be documented. New information that could impact a participant’s willingness to continue participation should be assessed to determine if re-consent is needed (e.g., depending on the stage of the trial, consideration should be given to whether the new information is relevant only to new participants or to existing participants). If re-consent is needed (e.g., information on emerging safety concerns), new information should be clearly identified in the revised informed consent materials. Revised informed consent materials should receive the IRB/IEC’s approval/favourable opinion in advance of use.
rows.location: III. Annex 1, 2.8.2 Informed Consent of Trial Participants
rows.review_note: Review: new row: missed by extraction. Double-check: passive; investigator actor inferred; long multi-part row.

f.title: Be able to perform emergency unblinding without undue delay from trial start

f.title: Ensure sufficient safety data support human exposure before the trial
f.statement: When planning trials, the sponsor should ensure that sufficient safety and efficacy data (nonclinical, clinical and/or real-world) are available to support human exposure by the route, dosages, duration and population to be studied.

f.title: Identify risks to critical-to-quality factors, including in computerised systems

f.title: Set quality tolerance limits and evaluate exceedances that may affect participant safety

f.statement: The protocol and, where applicable, protocol-related documents should describe how safety information will be collected from the various data sources (e.g. DHTs, in-person or remote visits), how data suggesting a potential safety concern will be identified and made available to the investigator in a timely manner, and what actions the investigator should take; the information should be provided so as to help inform the investigator's decisions (e.g. on eligibility, treatment, continued participation and participant safety).

f.title: Treat important medical events as serious
f.statement: An SAE is an unfavourable medical occurrence that results in death, is life-threatening, requires or prolongs hospitalisation, results in persistent or significant disability/incapacity or is a congenital anomaly/birth defect; important medical events that may jeopardise the participant or require intervention to prevent serious outcomes should generally be considered serious.
f.processes: Clinical safety monitoring; Medical review

rows.quote: Serious Adverse Event (SAE): Any unfavourable medical occurrence that is considered serious at any dose if it: • Results in death, • Is life-threatening, • Requires inpatient hospitalisation or prolongation of existing hospitalisation, • Results in persistent or significant disability/incapacity, or • Is a congenital anomaly/birth defect. (see ICH E2A) An important medical event that may not be immediately life-threatening or result in death or hospitalisation, that may jeopardise the participant or that may require intervention to prevent serious outcomes (see ICH E2A and E19) should generally be considered as serious.
rows.review_note: Review: no change. Double-check: glossary definition; level from 'should generally be considered'; actor inferred.

f.title: Classify SUSARs by the suspected, unexpected and serious criteria against the applicable product information
f.statement: A SUSAR is an adverse reaction that meets three criteria: suspected (a reasonable possibility that the drug caused the reaction), unexpected (nature or severity not consistent with the applicable product information, e.g. the IB or alternative documents per applicable requirements; see RSI) and serious (as defined for SAE).
f.clause: Glossary, Suspected Unexpected Serious Adverse Reaction (SUSAR)
f.processes: Clinical safety monitoring; Medical review; Reporting policy

rows.quote: Suspected Unexpected Serious Adverse Reaction (SUSAR): an adverse reaction that meets three criteria: suspected, unexpected and serious. • Suspected: There is a reasonable possibility that the drug caused the adverse drug reaction. 82 ICH E6(R3) Guideline • Unexpected: An adverse reaction, the nature or severity of which is not consistent with the applicable product information (e.g., Investigator’s Brochure or alternative documents according to applicable regulatory requirements; see RSI). • Serious: See above for SAE.
rows.location: Glossary, Suspected Unexpected Serious Adverse Reaction (SUSAR)
